query_plan.original_question: 最近三年MRI预测肝癌微血管侵犯有哪些研究？

ambiguities: 是否需要限定肝癌类型（如肝细胞癌）或分期？
是否需要限定MRI序列或对比剂类型（如普美显增强）？
是否需要限定研究类型（如原始研究或综述）？

preserved_constraints.text: 最近三年MRI预测肝癌微血管侵犯有哪些研究？

claims.text: 在所提供证据中，可找到多项以术前MRI预测肝细胞癌（HCC）微血管侵犯（MVI）为目标的原始研究，涵盖深度学习、影像组学、扩散MRI定量参数及人工神经网络等方法；这些研究均以术后病理MVI为参照，属于诊断/预测性研究，而非治疗性研究。
limitations: 证据均为摘要或部分全文片段，未提供完整研究清单，不能据此判断该领域全部研究数量。

claims.text: 深度学习方向：一项多中心研究构建基于对抗网络的深度学习模型（AD-DL），从多中心训练集中学习域不变特征，并与临床-影像模型及挤压激励网络模型比较；训练集263例（3个中心），内部验证66例，另设两个独立外部测试集。
limitations: 仅摘要，未提供网络结构、输入序列及训练细节。

claims.text: 影像组学与临床特征融合方向：一项研究纳入6个MRI序列，经跨序列配准后用深度神经网络分割HCC，再融合影像组学特征与单因素筛选的临床特征构建预测模型；另一项研究将MRI影像组学评分与血浆miRNA-21及肿瘤最大径结合构建列线图。
limitations: 两项研究均为摘要层面，列线图研究的具体MRI序列与影像组学流程未在摘要中说明。

claims.text: 扩散MRI定量参数方向：一项前瞻性研究在瘤内及3 mm、5 mm瘤周区域计算单指数DWI、IVIM、DKI、拉伸指数模型和连续时间随机游走模型参数，经逻辑回归筛选后结合AFP和肿瘤大小建模；另一项研究则利用多期增强MRI的跨期相特征变异，比较5种编码方法与4种机器学习分类器，并评估3、5、10 mm瘤周扩展。
limitations: 两项研究样本量分别为70例和115例，均为单中心回顾或前瞻队列，外部验证情况在摘要中未报告。

claims.text: 人工神经网络方向：一项研究对255例直径<3 cm的HCC患者T1加权平扫MRI进行肿瘤标注，以图像特征为输入构建三层ANN，并用bagging策略对50个分类器结果投票。
limitations: 仅摘要，未说明验证集划分方式。

claims.text: 多中心AD-DL模型在内部测试集AUC为0.793，外部测试集1为0.801，外部测试集2为0.773，为所比较模型中表现最佳；其MVI预测与早期无复发生存分层显著相关（p=0.048）。
limitations: 生存相关分析仅在外部测试集上进行，摘要未给出风险比等效应量。

claims.text: 6序列MRI影像组学+临床特征融合系统在420例HCC（140例MVI）中最高AUC为0.794±0.033，在3–5 cm肿瘤亚组AUC为0.860±0.065。
limitations: 亚组结果基于单中心回顾性数据，摘要未报告外部验证。

claims.text: 瘤周DWI研究中，单一参数以3 mm瘤周DKI Kapp判别最佳（AUROC=0.713），结合AFP与肿瘤大小的联合模型AUROC达0.844；作者报告瘤周DWI优于瘤内指标。
limitations: 样本量70例，联合模型性能可能受过拟合影响，摘要未报告校准或外部验证。

claims.text: 小肝癌（≤3 cm）跨期相MRI研究中，多期相模型一致优于单期相及仅用临床特征的模型；最佳组合为Fourier启发式时间编码+ExtraTrees、原始瘤内ROI加5 mm瘤周扩展，AUC为0.850（95% CI 0.675–0.978）。
limitations: 置信区间较宽，提示测试集样本量有限。

claims.text: ANN研究报道AUC为0.79，并发现肿瘤球形度与MVI显著相关（P<0.01），而AFP值与肿瘤体积与MVI无显著相关。
limitations: 相关性分析结果来自单中心小肿瘤人群，不能外推至较大肿瘤。

claims.text: MRI+miRNA影像基因组学列线图在验证队列（n=52）中AUC为0.900（95% CI 0.808–0.992），敏感度0.970、特异度0.722、准确度0.884、F1为0.916，高于任一单因素模型。
limitations: 验证队列样本量较小，且需血浆miRNA检测，增加了临床落地条件。

claims.text: 现有证据的方法学异质性明显：人群肿瘤大小范围不同（<3 cm、≤3 cm、3–5 cm亚组、未限大小），建模策略涵盖深度学习、影像组学、扩散定量参数与ANN，验证设置从单中心内部验证到多中心外部测试不等，因此不宜跨研究直接比较AUC或宣称某一方法优越。
limitations: 该判断基于所提供摘要与部分全文片段，未覆盖全部已发表研究。

claims.text: 所提供证据中，多数研究仅以摘要形式呈现，缺少模型校准、决策曲线（除列线图研究外）、前瞻性外部验证及报告规范等细节；这些信息在摘要层面未找到，而非证明原文缺失。
limitations: 无法从摘要判断全文是否报告了上述内容。

claims.text: 关于“最近三年”的时间限定，所提供证据未包含可核验的发表年份信息，因此无法在本回答中确认各研究是否均发表于近三年内。
limitations: 证据片段本身不含出版日期字段。

openalex_record.title: Interpretable and generalizable deep learning model for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion and outcome in hepatocellular carcinoma based on MRI: a multicenter study
openalex_record.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop an interpretable, domain-generalizable deep learning model for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective dataset of 546 HCC patients from five centers, we developed and validated a clinical-radiological model and deep learning models aimed at MVI prediction. The models were developed on a dataset of 263 cases consisting of data from three centers, internally validated on a set of 66 patients, and externally tested on two independent sets. An adversarial network-based deep learning (AD-DL) model was developed to learn domain-invariant features from multiple centers within the training set. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated using pathological MVI status. With the best-performed model, early recurrence-free survival (ERFS) stratification was validated on the external test set by the log-rank test, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with MVI status were tested on the RNA sequencing analysis of the Cancer Imaging Archive. RESULTS: The AD-DL model demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance and generalizability with an AUC of 0.793 in the internal test set, 0.801 in external test set 1, and 0.773 in external test set 2. The model's prediction of MVI status also demonstrated a significant correlation with ERFS (p = 0.048). DEGs associated with MVI status were primarily enriched in the metabolic processes and the Wnt signaling pathway, and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition process. CONCLUSIONS: The AD-DL model allows preoperative MVI prediction and ERFS stratification in HCC patients, which has a good generalizability and biological interpretability. CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: The adversarial network-based deep learning model predicts MVI status well in HCC patients and demonstrates good generalizability. By integrating bioinformatics analysis of the model's predictions, it achieves biological interpretability, facilitating its clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Current MVI assessment models for HCC lack interpretability and generalizability. The adversarial network-based model's performance surpassed clinical radiology and squeeze-and-excitation network-based models. Biological function analysis was employed to enhance the interpretability and clinical translatability of the adversarial network-based model.

sources.title: Interpretable and generalizable deep learning model for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion and outcome in hepatocellular carcinoma based on MRI: a multicenter study

evidence.text: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop an interpretable, domain-generalizable deep learning model for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective dataset of 546 HCC patients from five centers, we developed and validated a clinical-radiological model and deep learning models aimed at MVI prediction. The models were developed on a dataset of 263 cases consisting of data from three centers, internally validated on a set of 66 patients, and externally tested on two independent sets. An adversarial network-based deep learning (AD-DL) model was developed to learn domain-invariant features from multiple centers within the training set. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated using pathological MVI status. With the best-performed model, early recurrence-free survival (ERFS) stratification was validated on the external test set by the log-rank test, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with MVI status were tested on the RNA sequencing analysis of the Cancer Imaging Archive. RESULTS: The AD-DL model demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance and generalizability with an AUC of 0.793 in the internal test set, 0.801 in external test set 1, and 0.773 in external test set 2. The model's prediction of MVI status also demonstrated a significant correlation with ERFS (p = 0.048). DEGs associated with MVI status were primarily enriched in the metabolic processes and the Wnt signaling pathway, and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition process. CONCLUSIONS: The AD-DL model allows preoperative MVI prediction and ERFS stratification in HCC patients, which has a good generalizability and biological interpretability. CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: The adversarial network-based deep learning model predicts MVI status well in HCC patients and demonstrates good generalizability. By integrating bioinformatics analysis of the model's predictions, it achieves biological interpretability, facilitating its clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Current MVI assessment models for HCC lack interpretability and generalizability. The adversarial network-based model's performance surpassed clinical radiology and squeeze-and-excitation network-based models. Biological function analysis was employed to enhance the interpretability and clinical translatability of the adversarial network-based model.

openalex_record.title: Deep Neural Network and Radiomics-based Magnetic Resonance Imaging System for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
openalex_record.abstract: Background: Accurate preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is crucial for surgeons to make informed decisions regarding appropriate treatment strategies.However, it continues to pose a significant challenge for radiologists.The integration of computer-aided diagnosis utilizing deep learning technology emerges as a promising approach to enhance the prediction accuracy.Methods: This experiment incorporated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans with six different sequences.After a cross-sequence registration preprocess, a deep neural network was employed for the segmentation of hepatocellular carcinoma.The final prediction model was constructed by combining radiomics features with clinical features.The selection of clinical features for the final model was determined through univariate analysis.Results: In this study, we analyzed MRI scans obtained from a cohort of 420 patients diagnosed with HCC.Among them, 140 cases exhibited MVI, while the remaining 280 cases comprised the non-MVI group.The radiomics features demonstrated strong predictive capability for MVI.By extracting radiomic features from each MRI sequence and subsequently integrating them, we achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.794±0.033.Specifically, for tumor sizes ranging from 3 to 5 cm, the AUC reached 0.860±0.065.Conclusions: In this study, we present a fully automatic system for predicting MVI in HCC based on preoperative MRI.Our approach leverages the fusion of radiomics and clinical features to achieve accurate MVI prediction.The system demonstrates robust performance in predicting MVI, particularly in the 3-5 cm tumor group.

sources.title: Deep Neural Network and Radiomics-based Magnetic Resonance Imaging System for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma

evidence.text: Background: Accurate preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is crucial for surgeons to make informed decisions regarding appropriate treatment strategies.However, it continues to pose a significant challenge for radiologists.The integration of computer-aided diagnosis utilizing deep learning technology emerges as a promising approach to enhance the prediction accuracy.Methods: This experiment incorporated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans with six different sequences.After a cross-sequence registration preprocess, a deep neural network was employed for the segmentation of hepatocellular carcinoma.The final prediction model was constructed by combining radiomics features with clinical features.The selection of clinical features for the final model was determined through univariate analysis.Results: In this study, we analyzed MRI scans obtained from a cohort of 420 patients diagnosed with HCC.Among them, 140 cases exhibited MVI, while the remaining 280 cases comprised the non-MVI group.The radiomics features demonstrated strong predictive capability for MVI.By extracting radiomic features from each MRI sequence and subsequently integrating them, we achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.794±0.033.Specifically, for tumor sizes ranging from 3 to 5 cm, the AUC reached 0.860±0.065.Conclusions: In this study, we present a fully automatic system for predicting MVI in HCC based on preoperative MRI.Our approach leverages the fusion of radiomics and clinical features to achieve accurate MVI prediction.The system demonstrates robust performance in predicting MVI, particularly in the 3-5 cm tumor group.

openalex_record.title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI
openalex_record.abstract: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

sources.title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI

evidence.text: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

openalex_record.title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases
openalex_record.abstract: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. This study encoded feature variations across multi-phase MRI sequences for the preoperative prediction of MVI. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). All of them underwent preoperative MR examination and were randomly partitioned into training and testing cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. Radiomics features were subsequently extracted from both the original and expanded ROIs. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Among all evaluated combinations, the Fourier-inspired temporal encoding method combined with an ExtraTrees classifier, applied to the original tumoral ROI with a 5-mm peritumoral expansion, achieved the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.850 (95% CI: 0.675–0.978). Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

sources.title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases

evidence.text: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. This study encoded feature variations across multi-phase MRI sequences for the preoperative prediction of MVI. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). All of them underwent preoperative MR examination and were randomly partitioned into training and testing cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. Radiomics features were subsequently extracted from both the original and expanded ROIs. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Among all evaluated combinations, the Fourier-inspired temporal encoding method combined with an ExtraTrees classifier, applied to the original tumoral ROI with a 5-mm peritumoral expansion, achieved the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.850 (95% CI: 0.675–0.978). Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

openalex_record.title: Preoperative prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma microvascular invasion based on magnetic resonance imaging feature extraction artificial neural network
openalex_record.abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence is highly correlated with increased mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is indicative of aggressive tumor biology in HCC. AIM To construct an artificial neural network (ANN) capable of accurately predicting MVI presence in HCC using magnetic resonance imaging. METHODS This study included 255 patients with HCC with tumors < 3 cm. Radiologists annotated the tumors on the T1-weighted plain MR images. Subsequently, a three-layer ANN was constructed using image features as inputs to predict MVI status in patients with HCC. Postoperative pathological examination is considered the gold standard for determining MVI. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm. RESULTS Using the bagging strategy to vote for 50 classifier classification results, a prediction model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79. Moreover, correlation analysis revealed that alpha-fetoprotein values and tumor volume were not significantly correlated with the occurrence of MVI, whereas tumor sphericity was significantly correlated with MVI (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION Analysis of variable correlations regarding MVI in tumors with diameters < 3 cm should prioritize tumor sphericity. The ANN model demonstrated strong predictive MVI for patients with HCC (AUC = 0.79).

sources.title: Preoperative prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma microvascular invasion based on magnetic resonance imaging feature extraction artificial neural network

evidence.text: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence is highly correlated with increased mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is indicative of aggressive tumor biology in HCC. AIM To construct an artificial neural network (ANN) capable of accurately predicting MVI presence in HCC using magnetic resonance imaging. METHODS This study included 255 patients with HCC with tumors < 3 cm. Radiologists annotated the tumors on the T1-weighted plain MR images. Subsequently, a three-layer ANN was constructed using image features as inputs to predict MVI status in patients with HCC. Postoperative pathological examination is considered the gold standard for determining MVI. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm. RESULTS Using the bagging strategy to vote for 50 classifier classification results, a prediction model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79. Moreover, correlation analysis revealed that alpha-fetoprotein values and tumor volume were not significantly correlated with the occurrence of MVI, whereas tumor sphericity was significantly correlated with MVI (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION Analysis of variable correlations regarding MVI in tumors with diameters < 3 cm should prioritize tumor sphericity. The ANN model demonstrated strong predictive MVI for patients with HCC (AUC = 0.79).

openalex_record.title: Radiogenomics nomogram based on MRI and microRNAs to predict microvascular invasion of hepatocellular carcinoma
openalex_record.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to develop and validate a radiogenomics nomogram for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) on the basis of MRI and microRNAs (miRNAs). Materials and methods: This cohort study included 168 patients (training cohort: n = 116; validation cohort: n = 52) with pathologically confirmed HCC, who underwent preoperative MRI and plasma miRNA examination. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were used to identify independent risk factors associated with MVI. These risk factors were used to produce a nomogram. The performance of the nomogram was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis was performed to determine whether the nomogram was clinically useful. Results: The independent risk factors for MVI were maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21 (all P < 0.001). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score of the nomogram in the validation cohort were 0.970, 0.722, 0.884, and 0.916, respectively. The AUC of the nomogram was 0.900 (95% CI: 0.808-0.992) in the validation cohort, higher than that of any other single factor model (maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21). Conclusion: The radiogenomics nomogram shows satisfactory predictive performance in predicting MVI in HCC and provides a feasible and practical reference for tumor treatment decisions.

sources.title: Radiogenomics nomogram based on MRI and microRNAs to predict microvascular invasion of hepatocellular carcinoma

evidence.text: Purpose: This study aimed to develop and validate a radiogenomics nomogram for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) on the basis of MRI and microRNAs (miRNAs). Materials and methods: This cohort study included 168 patients (training cohort: n = 116; validation cohort: n = 52) with pathologically confirmed HCC, who underwent preoperative MRI and plasma miRNA examination. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were used to identify independent risk factors associated with MVI. These risk factors were used to produce a nomogram. The performance of the nomogram was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis was performed to determine whether the nomogram was clinically useful. Results: The independent risk factors for MVI were maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21 (all P < 0.001). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score of the nomogram in the validation cohort were 0.970, 0.722, 0.884, and 0.916, respectively. The AUC of the nomogram was 0.900 (95% CI: 0.808-0.992) in the validation cohort, higher than that of any other single factor model (maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21). Conclusion: The radiogenomics nomogram shows satisfactory predictive performance in predicting MVI in HCC and provides a feasible and practical reference for tumor treatment decisions.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of hepatocellular carcinoma microvascular invasion based on magnetic resonance imaging feature extraction artificial neural network
records.abstract: BACKGROUND Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) recurrence is highly correlated with increased mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is indicative of aggressive tumor biology in HCC. AIM To construct an artificial neural network (ANN) capable of accurately predicting MVI presence in HCC using magnetic resonance imaging. METHODS This study included 255 patients with HCC with tumors < 3 cm. Radiologists annotated the tumors on the T1-weighted plain MR images. Subsequently, a three-layer ANN was constructed using image features as inputs to predict MVI status in patients with HCC. Postoperative pathological examination is considered the gold standard for determining MVI. Receiver operating characteristic analysis was used to evaluate the effectiveness of the algorithm. RESULTS Using the bagging strategy to vote for 50 classifier classification results, a prediction model yielded an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.79. Moreover, correlation analysis revealed that alpha-fetoprotein values and tumor volume were not significantly correlated with the occurrence of MVI, whereas tumor sphericity was significantly correlated with MVI (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION Analysis of variable correlations regarding MVI in tumors with diameters < 3 cm should prioritize tumor sphericity. The ANN model demonstrated strong predictive MVI for patients with HCC (AUC = 0.79).

records.title: Deep Neural Network and Radiomics-based Magnetic Resonance Imaging System for Predicting Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
records.abstract: Background: Accurate preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is crucial for surgeons to make informed decisions regarding appropriate treatment strategies.However, it continues to pose a significant challenge for radiologists.The integration of computer-aided diagnosis utilizing deep learning technology emerges as a promising approach to enhance the prediction accuracy.Methods: This experiment incorporated magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans with six different sequences.After a cross-sequence registration preprocess, a deep neural network was employed for the segmentation of hepatocellular carcinoma.The final prediction model was constructed by combining radiomics features with clinical features.The selection of clinical features for the final model was determined through univariate analysis.Results: In this study, we analyzed MRI scans obtained from a cohort of 420 patients diagnosed with HCC.Among them, 140 cases exhibited MVI, while the remaining 280 cases comprised the non-MVI group.The radiomics features demonstrated strong predictive capability for MVI.By extracting radiomic features from each MRI sequence and subsequently integrating them, we achieved the highest area under the curve (AUC) value of 0.794±0.033.Specifically, for tumor sizes ranging from 3 to 5 cm, the AUC reached 0.860±0.065.Conclusions: In this study, we present a fully automatic system for predicting MVI in HCC based on preoperative MRI.Our approach leverages the fusion of radiomics and clinical features to achieve accurate MVI prediction.The system demonstrates robust performance in predicting MVI, particularly in the 3-5 cm tumor group.

records.title: Radiogenomics nomogram based on MRI and microRNAs to predict microvascular invasion of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Purpose: This study aimed to develop and validate a radiogenomics nomogram for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) on the basis of MRI and microRNAs (miRNAs). Materials and methods: This cohort study included 168 patients (training cohort: n = 116; validation cohort: n = 52) with pathologically confirmed HCC, who underwent preoperative MRI and plasma miRNA examination. Univariate and multivariate logistic regressions were used to identify independent risk factors associated with MVI. These risk factors were used to produce a nomogram. The performance of the nomogram was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC) analysis, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis was performed to determine whether the nomogram was clinically useful. Results: The independent risk factors for MVI were maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21 (all P < 0.001). The sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and F1-score of the nomogram in the validation cohort were 0.970, 0.722, 0.884, and 0.916, respectively. The AUC of the nomogram was 0.900 (95% CI: 0.808-0.992) in the validation cohort, higher than that of any other single factor model (maximum tumor length, rad-score, and miRNA-21). Conclusion: The radiogenomics nomogram shows satisfactory predictive performance in predicting MVI in HCC and provides a feasible and practical reference for tumor treatment decisions.

records.title: Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma and Its Prognostic Implications: A Multicenter Study
records.abstract: Introduction: Previous studies on preoperative predictors of microvascular invasion (MVI) in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICCA) have presented inconsistent results. This study aimed to identify preoperative clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) factors that can predict MVI in ICCA and to evaluate their prognostic utility using a multicenter cohort. Methods: A multicenter cohort of 446 patients who underwent preoperative MRI and surgical resection for ICCA at six tertiary referral institutions between 2009 and 2018 was analyzed for clinical, pathologic, and MR imaging characteristics. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify significant predictors of pathologically confirmed MVI, which were subsequently used to stratify patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups based on the number of predictors identified. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and log-rank test were conducted to assess long-term survival and early recurrence among the three groups. Results: Among the 446 patients (mean age, 63.0 ± 9.9 years; 277 men), 234 (52.5%) had MVI on pathology. Independent predictors of MVI included serum carbohydrate antigen 19–9 levels (≥80 U/mL; odds ratio [OR]: 2.68, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.64–4.37, p < 0.001), tumor size (≥4 cm; OR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.01–2.54, p = 0.046), tumor multiplicity (OR: 2.84, 95% CI: 1.58–5.12, p < 0.001), and arterial phase peritumoral enhancement (OR: 2.83, 95% CI: 1.81–4.42, p < 0.001). Stratifying patients by MVI risk – low (no predictors), intermediate (1–3 predictors), and high (4 predictors) – revealed a significant decrease in both recurrence-free and overall survival rates (p < 0.001), along with a corresponding increase in early recurrence rates (p < 0.001) as the risk level increased. Conclusion: Risk stratification utilizing four key predictors can effectively assess the risk of MVI in ICCA and is associated with postoperative outcomes.

records.title: Interpretable and generalizable deep learning model for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion and outcome in hepatocellular carcinoma based on MRI: a multicenter study
records.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to develop an interpretable, domain-generalizable deep learning model for microvascular invasion (MVI) assessment in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). METHODS: Utilizing a retrospective dataset of 546 HCC patients from five centers, we developed and validated a clinical-radiological model and deep learning models aimed at MVI prediction. The models were developed on a dataset of 263 cases consisting of data from three centers, internally validated on a set of 66 patients, and externally tested on two independent sets. An adversarial network-based deep learning (AD-DL) model was developed to learn domain-invariant features from multiple centers within the training set. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated using pathological MVI status. With the best-performed model, early recurrence-free survival (ERFS) stratification was validated on the external test set by the log-rank test, and the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) associated with MVI status were tested on the RNA sequencing analysis of the Cancer Imaging Archive. RESULTS: The AD-DL model demonstrated the highest diagnostic performance and generalizability with an AUC of 0.793 in the internal test set, 0.801 in external test set 1, and 0.773 in external test set 2. The model's prediction of MVI status also demonstrated a significant correlation with ERFS (p = 0.048). DEGs associated with MVI status were primarily enriched in the metabolic processes and the Wnt signaling pathway, and the epithelial-mesenchymal transition process. CONCLUSIONS: The AD-DL model allows preoperative MVI prediction and ERFS stratification in HCC patients, which has a good generalizability and biological interpretability. CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: The adversarial network-based deep learning model predicts MVI status well in HCC patients and demonstrates good generalizability. By integrating bioinformatics analysis of the model's predictions, it achieves biological interpretability, facilitating its clinical translation. KEY POINTS: Current MVI assessment models for HCC lack interpretability and generalizability. The adversarial network-based model's performance surpassed clinical radiology and squeeze-and-excitation network-based models. Biological function analysis was employed to enhance the interpretability and clinical translatability of the adversarial network-based model.

records.title: Preoperative evaluation of microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma with a radiological feature-based nomogram: a bi-centre study
records.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop a nomogram for preoperative assessment of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) based on the radiological features of enhanced CT and to verify two imaging techniques (CT and MRI) in an external centre. METHOD: A total of 346 patients were retrospectively included (training, n = 185, CT images; external testing 1, n = 90, CT images; external testing 2, n = 71, MRI images), including 229 MVI-negative patients and 117 MVI-positive patients. The radiological features and clinical information of enhanced CT images were analysed, and the independent variables associated with MVI in HCC were determined by logistic regression analysis. Then, a nomogram prediction model was constructed. External validation was performed on CT (n = 90) and MRI (n = 71) images from another centre. RESULTS: Among the 23 radiological and clinical features, size, arterial peritumoral enhancement (APE), tumour margin and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) were independent influencing factors for MVI in HCC. The nomogram integrating these risk factors had a good predictive effect, with AUC, specificity and sensitivity values of 0.834 (95% CI: 0.774-0.895), 75.0% and 83.5%, respectively. The AUC values of external verification based on CT and MRI image data were 0.794 (95% CI: 0.700-0.888) and 0.883 (95% CI: 0.807-0.959), respectively. No statistical difference in AUC values among training set and testing sets was found. CONCLUSION: The proposed nomogram prediction model for MVI in HCC has high accuracy, can be used with different imaging techniques, and has good clinical applicability.

records.title: Accuracy of artificial intelligence models integrating machine learning and deep learning in detecting microvascular invasion in liver cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
records.abstract: e16184 Background: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a global health challenge, ranking sixth in incidence and third in cancer-related mortality. Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a crucial prognostic marker influencing recurrence rates and survival. Accurate preoperative MVI detection can guide surgical planning but is limited by invasive histopathological exams and interobserver variability. This study evaluates the diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), in predicting MVI in HCC using imaging modalities such as CT, MRI, ultrasound, PET/CT, and histopathology. Methods: A systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines, covering studies from 2010 to 2023. Comprehensive searches were conducted across PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane Library, Google Scholar, European PMC, and BioMed Central. AI models were assessed for diagnostic accuracy using QUADAS-2 and Radiomics Quality Score (RQS). Metrics like the area under the curve (AUC), sensitivity, and specificity were analyzed. Results: This meta-analysis synthesized data from 51 studies, encompassing 6,257 records. DL models showed a pooled AUC of 0.84 (95% CI: 0.80–0.86), with sensitivity and specificity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.75–0.82) and 0.84 (95% CI: 0.79–0.88), respectively. ML models achieved a pooled AUC of 0.83 (95% CI: 0.80–0.86), sensitivity of 0.79 (95% CI: 0.71–0.85), and higher specificity of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.84–0.92). Across imaging modalities, MRI and CT-based models achieved pooled AUCs of 0.87 and 0.83 for DL and 0.85 and 0.82 for ML, respectively. Ultrasound-based models demonstrated higher specificity but slightly lower sensitivity. Models incorporating clinical features did not outperform purely radiomics-based approaches. Quality assessments revealed low bias risks in patient selection (88%), index tests (94%), and reference standards (98%). However, only 51% of studies addressed inter-scanner variability, and 55% incorporated calibration or resampling. The mean RQS was 40%, with 84% adhering to robust imaging protocols. Conclusions: AI models, particularly DL, exhibit robust accuracy in predicting MVI in HCC, showing promise for integration into clinical workflows. These tools could enable personalized preoperative planning, improving patient outcomes and reducing recurrence risks. Standardized protocols, prospective validation, and broader adoption of advanced AI methods are needed to ensure consistent clinical utility and cost-effectiveness.

records.title: All deaths follow recurrence, but not all recurrences are fatal: a retrospective cohort study of recurrence timing and survival after curative resection of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Background Postoperative recurrence is the main barrier to long-term survival after curative resection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Whether recurrence timing, rather than recurrence itself, distinguishes lethal from non-lethal trajectories remains unclear. Methods We analyzed 154 patients after curative HCC resection at a single centre. Preoperative circulating tumour cells (CTCs) were classified as epithelial, mixed, or mesenchymal (M-CTC); microvascular invasion (MVI) was graded M0-M2. We defined the dissemination axis (DA) as a composite of the preoperative M-CTC phenotype and postoperative pathological MVI grade. Because MVI is pathological, the complete DA can only be calculated after pathologic review, not before surgery. Early recurrence was defined as recurrence within 24 months. Overall survival (OS) and recurrence-free survival (RFS) were assessed with penalised Cox models, landmark and time-window analyses, competing-risk methods, and exploratory log-hazard mediation. Results Of 154 patients, 142 (92.2%) developed recurrence: 118 with early recurrence, 24 with late recurrence, and 12 remained recurrence-free. During the observed follow-up period, no deaths occurred without prior recurrence (0/154); 80 of 83 deaths (96.4%) were preceded by early recurrence. Median OS was 18.5 months for early recurrence and was not reached for late or non-recurrence groups (observed median survival, 49.0 and 39.5 months respectively). Across DA strata, 24-month recurrence rates increased from 22.2% (low risk) to 95-98% (high risk), while median OS decreased from 47 to 12 months. High DA status independently predicted poorer RFS (HR 3.72; 95% CI 2.28-6.07) and OS (HR 3.25; 95% CI 1.69-6.25). The effect was concentrated in the first 24 months. Early recurrence accounted for 27.5% of the log-hazard attenuation (95% CI 15.5-44.9%), but this exploratory analysis cannot establish causal mediation. 24-month RFS status discriminated subsequent OS (time-dependent AUCs 0.732-0.862). Conclusion In this exploratory single-centre retrospective cohort study, recurrence timing distinguished lethal from non-lethal outcomes. The DA, combining a preoperative CTC phenotype with the postoperative MVI grade, identified patients at high risk of 24-month early recurrence, supporting evaluation of risk-stratified surveillance and 24-month RFS as an early endpoint in perioperative HCC trials. Because no external validation was performed, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require independent validation before clinical use.

records.title: Primary Malignant Neoplasms of the Liver
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the sixth most common cancer worldwide and the third most common cause of cancer death. Characteristic imaging features, that is, arterial phase hyperenhancement and delayed washout, on contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or multiphase computed tomography scan, can yield a noninvasive diagnosis of HCC in most patients, although biopsy is needed in some cases. Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a neoplasm of the epithelium of the intra- or extrahepatic biliary tree. Risk factors and mechanisms underlying the development of intra versus extrahepatic CCA differ, and this chapter focuses on intrahepatic CCA. Almost all possible types of sarcoma have been reported as primary liver tumours. These include embryonal sarcoma, rhabdomyosarcoma, leiomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, and so on. A standardized management of these lesions is not available, partly because of the rarity of these lesions but also because they are aggressive tumours with a very poor prognosis.

records.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
records.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

records.title: LIVER CANCER DETECTION USING RESNET, SWIN TRANSFORMER AND CONVNEXT TINY NETWORKS
records.journal: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
records.abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. Another challenge is that slices from the same patient can be very similar, which may cause data leakage when splitting the data randomly. This study focuses on classifying liver CT slices into Tumor and No-Tumor classes using deep learning. The LiTS and 3Dircadb datasets are combined and used for the experiments. Three deep learning models, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50, are trained and evaluated. A patient-level data split is used to keep patients in the training, validation, and test sets separate. The three models are also combined using a soft-voting ensemble. The final evaluation is performed on an unseen test set containing 6,323 slices. The soft-voting ensemble achieved the highest accuracy of 92.74%. These results show that the models can detect tumor and no-tumor slices, while the class imbalance remains an important challenge for tumor detection.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI
records.abstract: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

records.title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases
records.abstract: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. This study encoded feature variations across multi-phase MRI sequences for the preoperative prediction of MVI. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). All of them underwent preoperative MR examination and were randomly partitioned into training and testing cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. Radiomics features were subsequently extracted from both the original and expanded ROIs. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Among all evaluated combinations, the Fourier-inspired temporal encoding method combined with an ExtraTrees classifier, applied to the original tumoral ROI with a 5-mm peritumoral expansion, achieved the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.850 (95% CI: 0.675–0.978). Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

records.title: A multiparametric liver MRI dataset with multiple tumor and liver segmentations of pre-treatment hepatocellular carcinomas
records.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays a key role for HCC screening, diagnosis and treatment planning, the development of AI models for detection and characterization of focal liver lesions is hindered by the scarcity of publicly available annotated MRI datasets. Here, we present OpenSwissHCC, a curated multiphasic dataset of 132 multiparametric DCE-MRI scans from adult patients with chronic liver disease acquired on 1.5 T and 3 T MRI scanners between 2011 and 2020. The dataset includes both HCC-positive (n = 63) and HCC-negative (n = 69) patients, with up to five lesions per patient segmented across each sequence when confidently identified. Whole-liver and lesion segmentations were manually performed and expert-validated, with lesion metadata including LI-RADS scores, size, liver segment location, major LI-RADS imaging features (non-rim APHE, washout, capsule, threshold growth) and key ancillary/background findings (e.g., mosaic architecture, fat/blood products, necrosis, tumor-in-vein; cirrhosis and portal-hypertension signs). In total, 140 lesions were annotated, including 97 confirmed HCC. Additionally, we provide liver masks for all T1-weighted images (T1-WI) sequences, generated using a pre-trained nnU-Net model, as well as pre-computed transforms to facilitate registration across T1-WI phases. By providing a comprehensive, well-annotated, and standardized collection of liver MRI examinations, OpenSwissHCC aims to assist the development and benchmarking of advanced computational methods for automated HCC detection, segmentation, and characterization, fostering progress toward precision imaging and personalized treatment planning.

records.title: Head-to-head comparison of [18F]FAPI and [18F]FDG PET/CT in the clinical value of hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: To investigate the clinical utility of fluorine-18-labeled fibroblast activation protein (FAP) inhibitor ([ 18 F]FAPI) positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) relative to [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose ([ 18 F]FDG) PET/CT for tumor detection and staging in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients. A cohort of 38 individuals (median age, 61 years; interquartile range, 56–68 years), all with pathologically confirmed primary or recurrent HCC, were enrolled. All participants underwent both [ 18 F]FDG and [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT. Maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax), tumor-to-background ratio (TBR), metabolic tumor volume (MTV), FAP expression tumor volume (FTV), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), total lesion FAP expression (TLF), and clinical staging were compared. Each patient had at least one intrahepatic lesion confirmed by surgical resection or percutaneous biopsy. Histopathologic confirmation was available for 46/66 intrahepatic lesions, 3/56 lymph-node (LN) metastases, and 4/33 distant metastases; the remaining lesions were adjudicated using a composite reference standard based on multimodal imaging follow-up and treatment response. Additionally, correlations between PET imaging findings and serum biomarkers, comprising alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II), were analyzed. The cohort included 32 primary and 6 recurrent HCC cases. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection rates than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic lesions (96.7% vs. 60.0%; p < 0.001), LN metastases (94.6% vs. 80.4%; p = 0.021), and distant metastases (78.8% vs. 48.5%; p = 0.002). For primary intrahepatic lesions, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.90 vs. 4.80, p < 0.001) and TBR (5.45 vs. 2.60, p < 0.001) than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT. In the patient-level volumetric analysis of the 32 initial-staging patients, FTV was 21.04 vs. MTV 13.75 ( p < 0.001), and TLF was 135.36 vs. TLG 51.44 ( p < 0.001). For LN metastases, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher SUVmax (7.98 vs. 6.63, p = 0.048) and TBR (7.85 vs. 4.95, p < 0.001), as well as higher FTV than MTV (6.55 vs. 4.55, p < 0.001) and TLF than TLG (67.65 vs. 52.75, p < 0.001). Positive correlations were observed between [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT tumor uptake parameters and AFP and PIVKA-II levels (nominal p < 0.05). Relative to [ 18 F]FDG, [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT produced staging changes in 19/32 patients undergoing initial staging, including 6 true upstagings, and identified 3 additional local recurrences; a FAPI-informed management change was implemented in 57.9% (22/38) of patients. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses yielded areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.947, 0.921, 0.895, and 0.864 for SUVmax, TBR, FTV, and TLF, respectively. [ 18 F]FAPI PET/CT showed higher lesion detection in selected HCC settings than [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT for primary intrahepatic, lymph-node, and distant metastatic lesions and may provide complementary information for staging and treatment planning in this preliminary single-center cohort. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05810324; registered on 30 March 2023.

records.title: Foundation Model‐Enabled Pathology‐Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
records.abstract: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model-enabled framework for pathology-informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole-slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI. PIVOT-MRI uses morphologic and vascular embedding alignment, and PIVOT-Clinical combines the PIVOT-MRI score with tumor size and alpha-fetoprotein. The multicenter retrospective study includes 2052 patients in a training cohort, an internal test cohort, and four external validation cohorts. PIVOT-MRI achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.887 in the internal test cohort and 0.839-0.861 across external cohorts. PIVOT-Clinical increases the internal-test area under the curve to 0.904 and PIVOT-Clinical-defined groups are associated with different two-year recurrence risks. Removing both histopathologic alignment branches results in the largest ablation-related performance decrease. Exploratory radiotranscriptomic analyses showed that higher PIVOT-MRI scores were associated with angiogenesis-related, endothelial, and proliferative transcriptional programs. PIVOT enables noninvasive preoperative assessment of pathology-defined vascular aggressiveness in resectable hepatocellular carcinoma while preserving an MRI-only clinical inference pathway.

records.abstract: Background The optimal resection margin width for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains controversial. The purpose of this study was to explore the value of preoperative circulating tumor cells (CTCs) status and tumor size in guiding the resection margin width of patients with HCC. Methods This study was a multicenter retrospective study that included 383 patients who underwent resection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Preoperative circulating tumor cell (CTC) detection (CTC ≥ 1/CTC = 0) and imaging evaluation of tumor size (≤ 3 cm/> 3 cm) were performed in all patients. We aimed to compare recurrence-free survival (RFS) and overall survival (OS) between patients receiving narrow (< 1 cm) and wide (≥ 1 cm) resection margins. Results Tumor diameter and CTC status were independent predictors of RFS and OS in the entire cohort. In patients with tumor diameter ≤ 3 cm, CTC-positive status correlated with poorer RFS but not OS. RFS and OS of narrow margin group and wide margin group were similar, and there was no statistical significance (P > 0.05). In the patients with tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-negative group, the RFS and OS of the narrow margin group were comparable to those of the wide margin group (P > 0.05). However, in patients with tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-positive groups, RFS and OS were better in the wide margin group than in the narrow margin group (P < 0.05). Conclusions Using preoperative CTC status and tumor diameter as preoperative markers, combined analysis of CTC status and tumor diameter could help to determine surgical margin width in patients with solitary HCC. Narrow margins are indicated for patients with a tumor diameter ≤ 3 cm (regardless of CTC status) and for patients with a tumor diameter > 3 cm and CTC-negative. Whereas wide margins are preferred in patients with tumors > 3 cm in diameter and CTC-positive.

records.title: Bi-regional dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI for prediction of microvascular invasion in solitary BCLC stage A hepatocellular carcinoma
records.abstract: Abstract Objectives To construct a combined model based on bi-regional quantitative dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI), as well as clinical-radiological (CR) features for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in solitary Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage A hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to assess its ability for stratifying the risk of recurrence after hepatectomy. Methods Patients with solitary BCLC stage A HCC were prospective collected and randomly divided into training and validation sets. DCE perfusion parameters were obtained both in intra-tumoral region (ITR) and peritumoral region (PTR). Combined DCE perfusion parameters (CDCE) were constructed to predict MVI. The combined model incorporating CDCE and CR features was developed and evaluated. Kaplan–Meier method was used to investigate the prognostic significance of the model and the survival benefits of different hepatectomy approaches. Results A total of 133 patients were included. Total blood flow in ITR and arterial fraction in PTR exhibited the best predictive performance for MVI with areas under the curve (AUCs) of 0.790 and 0.792, respectively. CDCE achieved AUCs of 0.868 (training set) and 0.857 (validation set). A combined model integrated with the α-fetoprotein, corona enhancement, two-trait predictor of venous invasion, and CDCE could improve the discrimination ability to AUCs of 0.966 (training set) and 0.937 (validation set). The combined model could stratify the prognosis of HCC patients. Anatomical resection was associated with a better prognosis in the high-risk group (p < 0.05). Conclusion The combined model integrating DCE perfusion parameters and CR features could be used for MVI prediction in HCC patients and assist clinical decision-making. Critical relevance statement The combined model incorporating bi-regional DCE-MRI perfusion parameters and CR features predicted MVI preoperatively, which could stratify the risk of recurrence and aid in optimizing treatment strategies. Key Points Microvascular invasion (MVI) is a significant predictor of prognosis for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Quantitative DCE-MRI could predict MVI in solitary BCLC stage A HCC; the combined model improved performance. The combined model could help stratify the risk of recurrence and aid treatment planning. records.title: Predicting the microvascular invasion and tumor grading of intrahepatic mass-forming cholangiocarcinoma based on magnetic resonance imaging radiomics and morphological features
records.journal: Quantitative Imaging in Medicine and Surgery
records.abstract: Background: Preoperative diagnosis of microvascular invasion (MVI) and tumor grading of intrahepatic mass-forming cholangiocarcinoma (IMCC) using imaging findings can facilitate patient treatment decision-making. This study was conducted to establish and validate nomograms based on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) radiomics and morphological features for predicting the MVI and tumor grading of IMCC before radical hepatectomy. Methods: A total of 235 patients with resected IMCC at the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College were divided into a training set (n=167) and a validation set (n=68), retrospectively. Clinical data and MRI morphological features were recorded. Univariate and multivariate analyses were conducted to identify the significant features for the prediction of MVI and tumor grading. Radiomics features were extracted from T2-weighted imaging fat-suppressed and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI). Radiomics signatures (rad_scores) were built based on the least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) method. Then, the nomograms were constructed by combining the rad_scores and the significant clinical or MRI morphologic features. The predictive performances for MVI and tumor grading were evaluated by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration, and clinical utility. Results: Totals of 16 and 9 radiomics features were selected to build the rad_scores for the prediction of MVI and tumor grading for the training and validation set, respectively. The nomogram for the prediction of MVI comprised the morphologic features including number of tumors, tumor margin, and rad_score. For the prediction of tumor grading, the nomogram comprised the number of tumors, tumor necrosis, and rad_score. The best discriminations were observed in the training and validation sets for the MVI nomogram [AUCs of 0.874, 95% confidence interval (CI): (0.822-0.926) and 0.869 (0.783-0955)] and tumor grading nomogram [AUCs of 0.827 (0.763-0.891) and 0.848 (0.759-0.937)]. Decision curve analysis (DCA) further confirmed the clinical utilities of the nomograms. Conclusions: Nomograms based on MRI radiomics and morphological features can effectively predict the individualized risks of MVI and tumor grading for IMCC.

records.title: Radiomics of Preoperative Multi-Sequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging Can Improve the Predictive Performance of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
records.abstract: Background: The aim of the study is to demonstrate that radiomics of preoperative multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can indeed improve the predictive performance of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods: A total of 206 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC who underwent preoperative enhanced MRI were retrospectively recruited. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the independent clinicoradiologic predictors of MVI present and constituted the clinicoradiologic model. Recursive feature elimination (RFE) was applied to select radiomics features (extracted from six sequence images) and constructed the radiomics model. Clinicoradiologic model plus radiomics model formed the clinicoradiomics model. Five-fold cross-validation was used to validate the three models. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were used to evaluate the performance. Net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to compare the prediction accuracy between models. Results: The clinicoradiologic model contained alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)_lg10, radiological capsule enhancement, enhancement pattern and arterial peritumoral enhancement, which were independent risk factors of MVI. There were 18 radiomics features related to MVI constructed the radiomics model. The mean area under the receiver operating curve (AUC) of clinicoradiologic, radiomics and clinicoradiomics model were 0.849, 0.925 and 0.950 in the training cohort and 0.846, 0.907 and 0.933 in the validation cohort, respectively. The three models' calibration curves fitted well, and decision curve analysis (DCA) confirmed the clinical usefulness. Compared with the clinicoradiologic model, the NRI of radiomics and clinicoradiomics model increased significantly by 0.575 and 0.825, respectively, and the IDI increased significantly by 0.280 and 0.398, respectively. Conclusions: Radiomics of preoperative multi-sequence MRI can improve the predictive performance of MVI in HCC.

records.title: Diagnostic value of a model combining contrast-enhanced ultrasound, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance imaging parameters for microvascular invasion in renal cell carcinoma
records.abstract: Objectives: To evaluate the diagnostic value of combined contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS), computed tomography (CT), and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) parameters for detecting microvascular invasion (MVI) in renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Methods: From January 2024 to December 2025, the clinical records of RCC patients treated in a hospital in East China were retrospectively collected. Among them, 52 patients with MVI were included in the MVI group. Using propensity score matching (ratio 1:1), 52 patients without MVI were included in the non-MVI group. All patients underwent CEUS, CT, and MRI examinations. The differences in examination parameters between the two groups were compared. The diagnostic value of those parameters for RCC-MVI was analyzed. Results: Compared with the non-MVI group, the MVI group had shorter time to peak, initial enhancement time, and washout time, higher kurtosis, entropy, maximum apparent diffusion coefficient (ADCmax), and minimum ADC (ADCmin), and lower energy parameters (all P < 0.001). ROC curve analysis showed that the AUC values of time to peak, initial enhancement time, washout time, kurtosis, energy, entropy, ADCmax, and ADCmin for diagnosing RCC-MVI were 0.791, 0.856, 0.874, 0.789, 0.873, 0.898, 0.855, and 0.884, respectively, with sensitivities of 82.69%, 80.77%, 73.08%, 71.15%, 78.85%, 86.54%, 86.54%, and 86.54%, respectively. The AUC of the combined strategy was 0.966. Conclusion: The combination of CEUS, CT, and MRI parameters showed promising preliminary performance for identifying MVI in RCC. Further internal and external validation is required before the model can be considered for clinical application.

records.title: Decision-Tree Models Indicative of Microvascular Invasion on MRI Predict Survival in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma Following Tumor Ablation
records.abstract: Purpose: Histological microvascular invasion (MVI) is a risk factor for poor survival and early recurrence in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after surgery. Its prognostic value in the setting of locoregional therapies (LRT), where no tissue samples are obtained, remains unknown. This study aims to establish CT-derived indices indicative of MVI on liver MRI with superior soft tissue contrast and evaluate their association with patient survival after ablation via interstitial brachytherapy (iBT) versus iBT combined with prior conventional transarterial chemoembolization (cTACE). Patients and Methods: Ninety-five consecutive patients, who underwent ablation via iBT alone (n = 47) or combined with cTACE (n = 48), were retrospectively included between 01/2016 and 12/2017. All patients received contrast-enhanced MRI prior to LRT. Overall (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), and time-to-progression (TTP) were assessed. Decision-tree models to determine Radiogenomic Venous Invasion (RVI) and Two-Trait Predictor of Venous Invasion (TTPVI) on baseline MRI were established, validated on an external test set (TCGA-LIHC), and applied in the study cohorts to investigate their prognostic value for patient survival. Statistics included Fisher’s exact and t -test, Kaplan–Meier and cox-regression analysis, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC-ROC) and Pearson’s correlation. Results: OS, PFS, and TTP were similar in both treatment groups. In the external dataset, RVI showed low sensitivity but relatively high specificity (AUC-ROC = 0.53), and TTPVI high sensitivity but only low specificity (AUC-ROC = 0.61) for histological MVI. In patients following iBT alone, positive RVI and TTPVI traits were associated with poorer OS (RVI: p < 0.01; TTPVI: p = 0.08), PFS (p = 0.04; p = 0.04), and TTP (p = 0.14; p = 0.03), respectively. However, when patients with combined cTACE and iBT were stratified by RVI or TTPVI, no differences in OS (p = 0.75; p = 0.55), PFS (p = 0.70; p = 0.43), or TTP (p = 0.33; p = 0.27) were observed. Conclusion: The study underscores the role of non-invasive imaging biomarkers indicative of MVI to identify patients, who would potentially benefit from embolotherapy via cTACE prior to ablation rather than ablation alone. Keywords: cancer imaging, hepatocellular carcinoma, microvascular invasion, magnetic resonance tomography, predictive imaging biomarkers

records.title: Radiomics-Based Prediction of Microvascular Invasion Grade in Nodular Hepatocellular Carcinoma Using Contrast-Enhanced Magnetic Resonance Imaging
records.abstract: Objective: The aim of this study is to develop and verify a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based radiomics model for predicting the microvascular invasion grade (MVI) before surgery in individuals diagnosed with nodular hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods: A total of 198 patients were included in the study and were randomly stratified into two groups: a training group consisting of 139 patients and a test group comprising 59 patients. The tumor lesion was manually segmented on the largest cross-sectional slice using ITK SNAP, with agreement reached between two radiologists. The selection of radiomics features was carried out using the LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) algorithm. Radiomics models were then developed through maximum correlation, minimum redundancy, and logistic regression analyses. The performance of the models in predicting MVI grade was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and metrics derived from the confusion matrix. Results: There were no notable statistical differences in sex, age, BMI (body mass index), tumor size, and location between the training and test groups. The AP and PP radiomic model constructed for predicting MVI grade demonstrated an AUC of 0.83 (0.75-0.88) and 0.73 (0.64-0.80) in the training group and an AUC of 0.74 (0.61-0.85) and 0.62 (0.48-0.74) in test group, respectively. The combined model consists of imaging data and clinical data (age and AFP), achieved an AUC of 0.85 (0.78-0.91) and 0.77 (0.64-0.87) in the training and test groups, respectively. Conclusion: A radiomics model utilizing-contrast-enhanced MRI demonstrates strong predictive capability for differentiating MVI grades in individuals with nodular HCC. This model could potentially function as a dependable and resilient tool to support hepatologists and radiologists in their preoperative decision-making processes.

records.title: Surgical resection combined with TACE for primary clear cell carcinoma of the liver: a case report and literature review
records.abstract: Background Primary clear cell carcinoma of the liver (PCCCL) is an uncommon hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) subtype that resembles extrahepatic clear cell tumors, posing diagnostic challenges. Case presentation A 74-year-old woman with hepatitis B–related cirrhosis (Child-Pugh class A) presented with acute abdominal pain and vomiting. Imaging revealed a hypervascular hepatic lesion with intralesional fat, while serum AFP was normal and CA125 mildly elevated. Laparoscopic partial hepatectomy was performed. Histology confirmed PCCCL, and immunohistochemistry supported hepatic origin while excluding metastatic renal carcinoma. The patient subsequently received two sessions of postoperative TACE as an individualized treatment and remained free of recurrence or metastasis during surveillance from 2022 to 2025. Conclusion PCCCL is rare and difficult to distinguish from conventional HCC or metastatic clear cell carcinoma. Histopathology with immunohistochemistry is essential for diagnosis. Surgical resection is the mainstay of treatment. Although this patient remained recurrence-free after postoperative TACE, the role of TACE cannot be determined based on a single case, and studies with larger sample sizes are still needed.

records.title: Liver transplantation for hepatocellular carcinoma: Mechanisms, risk stratification, and evolving treatment landscape
records.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), remains a leading cause of mortality.This article addresses the mechanisms underlying post-transplant HCC recurrence and evaluates current evidence-based strategies for diagnosis and management.Based on a targeted narrative review of high-impact literature published between 2010 and 2025, we synthesize evidence on the interplay between immunosuppression, tumor biology, and host-related factors driving recurrence.Using HCC recurrence after liver transplantation as the principal model, we critically examine existing risk stratification systems and surveillance protocols.We further summarize multimodal therapeutic approaches, ranging from curativeintent local therapies for oligo-recurrence to systemic treatments for advanced stages, where prognosis remains poor.Additionally, we discuss the emerging and controversial role of adjuvant therapies in high-risk populations.The review highlights areas of consensus, ongoing controversies, and key gaps in knowledge that require further investigation to improve long-term post-transplant outcomes.Particular attention is given to the role of immunosuppressive regimen modulation and emerging biomarker-driven surveillance strategies aimed at earlier detection and individualized risk prediction in post-transplant patients to ultimately improve survival and clinical decision-making.
